trinidad-dr--espiritu.description: Trinidad Espiritu opened a planned three-part series from Altadis U.S.A. in 2019, made by AJ Fernández in Estelí as a Nicaraguan puro. Its theme looks back to Caribbean cigar culture of the late 1960s and early 1970s, when Trinidad was first rolled in Havana. Medium in strength, it brings nuts, earth, coffee and pepper over a light fruit sweetness.

thirds.notes: Pepper on the first puffs gives way to nuts, earth and coffee, with a little chocolate and fruity sweetness.
Earth moves to the front as the sweetness fades; spice and leather build, with a citrus thread for some.
Earth and natural tobacco lead to the close with pepper, coffee, leather and darker spice; the finish can turn harsh.

trinidad-dr--espiritu-series-no-2.description: Espiritu Series No. 2, announced by Altadis U.S.A. for a January 2020 debut, honours Brazil with the colours of its flag on box and band. Blended by AJ Fernández and Rafael Nodal, it pairs Brazilian and Nicaraguan tobaccos. The smoke is dark and sweet, with chocolate and espresso, orange peel and nutmeg, and a peppery edge.

thirds.notes: Sweet dark chocolate and espresso open with orange and strong black pepper, then orange peel and nutmeg settle in.
The orange returns a little as the nutmeg softens; chocolate and espresso carry the finish while the body fills out.
The citrus falls away and the chocolate loses some sweetness, leaving espresso and nutmeg to the end.

sources.title: Tiny Tim's Blog – Trinidad Espiritu No. 2 Toro
JR Cigars Blending Room – Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 2

trinidad-dr--espiritu-series-no-3.description: The third Espiritu, released at the end of October 2023 for the Day of the Dead, honours Mexico with a San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. AJ Fernández and Rafael Nodal blended it, and it is rolled at Fernández's factory in Estelí. Medium-full, it centres on chocolate and espresso, with pepper, earth and a faint dark fruit.

thirds.notes: Chocolate leads with coffee, white pepper and a touch of fruit, while the retrohale brings black pepper and earth.
The flavours deepen: espresso firms up beside cocoa and pepper, and roasted nuts and sweeter spice appear.
Coffee joins chocolate up front, roasted earth steadies the close and pepper stays just behind.

trinidad-dr--espiritu-miami.description: Espiritu Miami is a limited edition honouring the city, unveiled by Altadis U.S.A. at the 2025 PCA show as a single 6 1/8 x 52 belicoso and capped at 4,000 boxes of 20. Like the first Espiritu, it is a Nicaraguan puro from AJ Fernández's factory. Citrus peel, brown sugar and black coffee lead, turning more bitter as it burns.

thirds.notes: Citrus peel and a peach-like fruit meet brown sugar, earth, a little caramel and black coffee, with lingering pepper.
Citrus peel still leads as the coffee grows stronger and some bitterness creeps in.
Black coffee dominates and the peel turns bitter, no longer balanced by the brown sugar.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Trinidad Espiritu Miami Edition to debut at PCA 2025

trinidad-dr--trinidad-x-tommy-bahama-isl.description: Announced in July 2025, this collaboration between Trinidad and the Tommy Bahama lifestyle brand is a Nicaraguan puro, blended by Rafael Nodal and AJ Fernández from tobacco grown on Fernández's own farms. It comes as Harbor, Breeze and Marlin in coastal-themed boxes. A sweet lemon note sits over earth, leather and black coffee, lifted by cedar, vanilla and pepper.

thirds.notes: Candy-like lemon and brown sugar over earth, leather and black coffee, with a pepper-heavy finish.
Earth turns heavy and pushes the lemon back, though it lingers on the finish with pepper.
Sweet lemon returns to the front as the earth recedes, with intense pepper on the finish.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – Trinidad x Tommy Bahama Island Collection announcement
Tiny Tim's Blog – Trinidad x Tommy Bahama Island Collection Breeze

trinidad-dr--paradox.description: Trinidad Paradox, now discontinued, was a box-pressed cigar from Altadis U.S.A. with a Mexican San Andrés Criollo '98 wrapper, a Dominican binder and Nicaraguan filler, offered as robusto, toro, belicoso and churchill. Mild in strength and medium in body, it smokes smooth and woody, with sweet syrup, leather, coffee and a nutmeg-like spice for any hour.

thirds.notes: Syrupy sweetness with leather and cedar, joined by smooth coffee and nuts; early pepper fades into baking spice.
Wood takes over and the smoke grows smoother, with light nutmeg or a sharper spice as the sweetness recedes.
Little new arrives: spice and leather carry to the close, with a touch of malty sweetness near the nub.

sources.title: Best Cigar Prices – Trinidad Paradox Toro review

trinidad-dr--santiago.description: Trinidad Santiago was the brand's first all-Dominican puro, developed by Rafael Nodal with Altadis U.S.A. and blended by José "Jochy" Blanco from Cibao Valley tobacco under a dark, oily Dominican wrapper. Medium-full in strength and body, it layers cocoa, spice, leather and toasted almonds before a peppery finish.
